raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary

Fix PIECEWISE CUDA graph execution with PCP by using persistent PCP input buffers during graph capture and sizing graph dispatch from the largest real rank-local PCP batch before padding.

## Implementation

- Decoder graph capture now uses `PCPManager.input_buffers` when PCP is active, ensuring capture and runtime partitioning share persistent `input_ids`, `positions`, and `is_padding` buffers.
- `GPUModelRunner` obtains the graph dispatch size from `PCPManager.get_num_tokens_for_dispatch()`.
- The CUDA graph dispatcher selects the smallest captured token size covering that rank-local maximum.
- The selected `BatchExecutionDescriptor.num_tokens` is passed to PCP partitioning as `padded_num_tokens`, which determines rank-local gather-index and mask capacity.
- A shared `_iter_rank_chunks()` implements rank chunking for both dispatch-size calculation and segment construction.
- PCP raises `ValueError` when `padded_num_tokens` is smaller than the largest rank-local batch.

Representative dispatch mappings:

| Workload | Global tokens | Rank-local maximum | Capture size |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| PCP2 prefill | 8 | 4 | 4 |
| PCP2 prefill | 7 | 4 | 4 |
| PCP2, 3 decodes | 3 | 3 | 4 |
| PCP2, 3 decodes + prefill | 11 | 7 | 8 |
| PCP4, 2 decodes + prefill | 11 | 5 | 8 |

## Validation configuration

- NVIDIA H20 GPUs
- GLM-4.7-Flash
- TP1 + PCP4 + EP4
- `max_num_batched_tokens=1024`
- `max_num_seqs=32`
- `max_model_len=8192`
- `gpu_memory_utilization=0.80`
- GSM8K 5-shot, temperature 0, seed 42, maximum output tokens 4096, concurrency 32
- PR head: `1dfcbc289db596b38052c33606a6f32c09d65ee9`
- Validation used the image-aligned FlashMLA Python runtime file; the source changes under test were exactly the PR head.

All four ranks completed 11/11 PIECEWISE graph captures. The service remained healthy after the full run, and logs contained zero graph replay, CUDA error, input-address mismatch, illegal-memory, traceback, engine-dead, initialization-failure signatures.

## Correctness results

| Scope | Revision | Mode | Correct | Accuracy | Invalid | Errors | Completion tokens |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 32-question smoke | PR head | Eager | 24/32 | 75.000% | 0 | 0 | 3,139 |
| 32-question smoke | PR head | PIECEWISE | 25/32 | 78.125% | 0 | 0 | 3,162 |
| Full GSM8K | PR head | Eager | 1085/1319 | 82.2593% | 0 | 0 | 136,925 |
| Full GSM8K | PR head | PIECEWISE | 1073/1319 | 81.3495% | 0 | 0 | 140,111 |
| Full GSM8K | Main baseline (`d626108b1841888ec90aced33367149a6bbc7e4b`) | PIECEWISE | 1037/1319 | 78.6202% | 1 | 0 | 364,147 |

For the paired PR-head full runs, 50 questions were correct only in Eager, 38 only in PIECEWISE, and 1,188 produced the same prediction. The exact McNemar p-value was `0.24079312453900145`.

## Test coverage

- `pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_pcp_manager.py`: 8 passed, 1 warning in 7.72s
- Covers PCP2 and PCP4 prefill, decode, mixed batches, replicated-decode PIECEWISE padding, the graph-capacity guard, and the PCP capture-buffer contract.
- Ruff check, Ruff format check, `compileall`, and `git diff --check` passed.

nodes.body: I opened #53639 as a draft alternative for comparing a materially different dispatch order. This PR selects a CUDA graph from the global scheduled token count and preserves that width through PCP partitioning. #53639 instead computes the exact maximum PCP-local width before graph dispatch, keeps global input staging separate, and pads each rank only to the selected local graph bucket. For PCP=4 with a 1024-token pure prefill, that changes the per-rank graph width from 1024 to 256; replicated decode widths remain unchanged. Only one implementation should merge.

> I opened https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53639 as a draft alternative for comparing a materially different dispatch order.

Dispatching with the actual tokens sharded by PCP is more beneficial. I’ve migrated some of the changes from #53639 and verified the accuracy.
